title: The Tragedy of the Cognitive Commons: How AI Could Disrupt the Regeneration of Professional Expertise
excerpt: Artificial intelligence is reshaping cognitive work, but Human Resource Development scholarship has treated this transformation as an organizational training challenge, leaving the collective regeneration of professional expertise unexamined. This conceptual paper introduces the Cognitive Commons framework, integrating commons theory, HRD scholarship, and distributed cognition to explain how rational AI adoption decisions can deplete the shared expertise pool professions require for renewal. The framework distinguishes Internalized Mastery (deep domain knowledge from sustained practice) from Distributed Mastery (orchestrating human-AI systems), and develops the Validation Tether: effective AI oversight depends on the expertise AI adoption may undermine. Early labor market and clinical evidence suggests possible disruption to expertise-regeneration pathways in highly AI-exposed sectors, though adoption is recent and the strongest signals come from leading sectors rather than all professions. Five factors determine occupational vulnerability, and governance arrangements may form across organizational, professional-association, and policy levels. The paper reframes expertise development as collective stewardship rather than organizational optimization, with implications for HRD theory and workforce policy.

摘要：人工智能正在重塑认知工作，但人力资源开发学术界将这种转变视为组织培训挑战，而没有审视专业知识的集体再生。 这篇概念性论文介绍了认知共享框架，整合了共享理论、人力资源开发奖学金和分布式认知，以解释合理的人工智能采用决策如何耗尽职业更新所需的共享专业知识库。 该框架将内部化掌握（来自持续实践的深层领域知识）与分布式掌握（编排人类人工智能系统）区分开来，并开发了验证系绳：有效的人工智能监督取决于人工智能采用可能破坏的专业知识。 早期劳动力市场和临床证据表明，高度人工智能化行业的专业知识再生途径可能会受到干扰，尽管人工智能的采用是最近才发生的，而且最强烈的信号来自领先行业而不是所有职业。 有五个因素决定职业脆弱性，治理安排可能会在组织、专业协会和政策层面形成。 该论文将专业知识发展重新定义为集体管理而不是组织优化，这对人力资源开发理论和劳动力政策具有影响。
